rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet named the surah Sūrat al-Nās, using its opening words.
rows.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سمى سورة الناس : { قل أعوذ برب الناس }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two protective surahs are called al-Muʿawwidhatayn and al-Mushaqshiqatan, with the shins preceding the qāfs in the latter name.
rows.anchor: تسميان ( المعوذتين ) ، و ( المشقشقتين )

rows.speaker: الزمخشري والقرطبي
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī and al-Qurṭubī also report the name al-Muqashqishtayn, with the qāfs preceding the shins.
rows.anchor: الزمخشري والقرطبي ذكر أنهما تسميان

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya titled it “the second protective surah,” construing the phrase as an adjective annexed to its described noun.
rows.anchor: ( المحرر الوجيز ) ( سورة المعوذة الثانية ) بإضافة ( سورة ) إلى

rows.speaker: الترمذي
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhī titled the pair al-Muʿawwidhatayn.
rows.anchor: وعنونهما الترمذي ( المعوذتين ) ، وعنونها البخاري

rows.speaker: البخاري
rows.claim: Al-Bukhārī titled it “Sūrat Qul aʿūdhu bi-rabbi al-nās.”
rows.anchor: وعنونها البخاري في ( صحيحه ) ( سورة قل أعوذ برب الناس )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Older and current Maghribi and Mashriqi muṣḥafs, along with most commentaries, call it Sūrat al-Nās.
rows.anchor: وفي مصاحفنا القديمة والحديثة المغربية والمشرقية تسمية هذه السورة ( سورة الناس ) وكذلك أكثر كتب التفسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some call it Meccan and others Medinan according to their view of al-Falaq; Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers that both descended in succession, so their classification disputes coincide.
rows.anchor: في سورة الفلق إنها مكية ، ومدنية في قول الذين قالوا

rows.speaker: الإتقان
rows.claim: Al-Itqān attributes the surah’s occasion to the magic of Labīd ibn al-Aʿṣam and says it descended with al-Falaq.
rows.anchor: وقال في ( الإتقان ) : إن سبب نزولها قصة سحر لبيد بن الأعصم

rows.speaker: القرطبي والواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī and al-Wāḥidī preceded al-Itqān in reporting the same occasion of revelation.
rows.anchor: وقد سبقه إلى ذلك القرطبي والواحدي ، وقد علمت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr says he has already refuted the magic report in his discussion of al-Falaq.
rows.anchor: وقد علمت تزييفه في سورة الفلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the preferred Meccan dating, it is the twenty-first surah, revealed after al-Falaq and before al-Ikhlāṣ.
rows.anchor: الحادية والعشرين من السور ، نزلت عقب سورة الفلق وقبل سورة الإخلاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah has six verses.
rows.anchor: وعدد آيها ست آيات

rows.speaker: الإتقان
rows.claim: Al-Itqān mentions a seven-verse count, which Ibn ʿĀshūr notes is not attributed to the recognized authorities on verse counting.
rows.anchor: قولا : إنها سبع آيات وليس معزوا لأهل العدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah instructs the Prophet to seek refuge from the whisperer’s evil, which seeks to corrupt his work and guidance and turn people away from his call.
rows.anchor: إرشاد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لأن يتعوذ بالله ربه من شر الوسواس الذي يحاول إفساد عمل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وإفساد إرشاده الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command implies that God will protect the Prophet from the whisperer and preserve his mission until it reaches the people.
rows.anchor: إلى أن الله تعالى معيذه من ذلك فعاصمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The instruction also teaches Muslims to seek this refuge, with protection from whispering proportionate to their spiritual rank.
rows.anchor: فيكون لهم من هذا التعوذ ما هو حظهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Falaq seeks refuge from evils of creatures, animals, and people, whereas al-Nās seeks refuge from hidden creatures, the satans.
rows.anchor: سورة الفلق تعوذ من شرور المخلوقات من حيوان وناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As with al-Falaq, the command to speak is addressed to the Prophet while its intended scope includes his community.
rows.anchor: الخطاب للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم والمقصود شموله أمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is called the Lord of people because satanic evil enters their hearts and misguides both its targets and those they may mislead; invoking their Lord asks Him to restrain the aggressor and protect the victim.
rows.anchor: وعرف { رب } بإضافته إلى { الناس } دون غيرهم من المربوبين لأن الاستعاذة من شر يلقيه الشيطان في قلوب الناس فيضلون ويضلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine descriptions progress from creating humans, to ruling them, to being their deity, showing that His lordship and authority are unlike those of one human over another.
rows.anchor: ثم هم غير خارجين عن حكمه إذا شاء أن يتصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order also traces knowledge of God: awareness of a Lord begins with one’s existence and constitution, deepens to recognition of the true, self-sufficient King, and ends in knowing Him as the one deserving worship.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا الترتيب إشعار أيضا بمراتب النظر في معرفة الله تعالى فإن الناظر يعلم بادىء ذي بدء بأن له ربا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “King of people” and “God of people” are explanatory appositions to “Lord of people”; repeating “people” instead of using a pronoun lets each clarified name stand independently, as an apposition does.
rows.anchor: و { ملك الناس } عطف بيان من { رب الناس } وكذلك { إله الناس } فتكرير لفظ { الناس } دون اكتفاء بضميره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-nās is a collective noun for all human beings or a group among them, and, strictly speaking, is not used for anything other than humans.
rows.anchor: اسم جمع للبشر جميعهم أو طائفة منهم ولا يطلق على غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-waswās means one who whispers, and waswasa is hidden speech.
rows.anchor: الوسواس } : المتكلم بالوسوسة ، وهي الكلام الخفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ruʾba uses the verb waswasa in a line about calling upon the Lord of daybreak, illustrating the term’s usage.
rows.anchor: وسوس يدعو مخلصا رب الفلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-waswās is an active participle; with an open wāw it can metaphorically mean thoughts a person imagines as self-addressed speech.
rows.anchor: فالوسواس اسم فاعل ويطلق الوسواس بفتح الواو مجازا على ما يخطر بنفس المرء من الخواطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr cites ʿUrwa ibn Udhayna’s verse, where sawāwis names consoling thoughts that the heart refers to the conscience.
rows.anchor: وإذا وجدت لها وساوس سلوة شفع الفؤاد إلى الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite al-waswās is generic and covers both literal and figurative whispering: satanic thoughts of evil and human secret conspiracies.
rows.anchor: والتعريف في { الوسواس } تعريف الجنس وإطلاق { الوسواس } على معنييه المجازي والحقيقي يشمل الشياطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan is included because it instills evil thoughts in people; the Qurʾānic example is Satan whispering to Adam.
rows.anchor: فوسوس إليه الشيطان } ( طه : 120 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human whisperers include plotters who secretly plan murder, theft, or enticement into misguidance, including people conspiring against the Messenger and urging harm to him.
rows.anchor: ويشمل الوسواس كل من يتكلم كلاما خفيا من الناس وهم أصحاب المكائد والمؤامرات المقصود منها إلحاق الأذى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-khannās is an emphatic or intensive form describing one for whom withdrawal and concealment have become habitual; khunūs means disappearing.
rows.anchor: الشديد الخنس والكثيره . والمراد أنه صار عادة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan is called al-khannās because it reaches a person’s reason and resolve unnoticed; schemers are also hidden, exploiting people’s inattention through tricks.
rows.anchor: والشيطان يلقب ب { الخناس } لأنه يتصل بعقل الإنسان وعزمه من غير شعور منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in al-khannās matches the generic definiteness of its described noun, al-waswās.
rows.anchor: فالتعريف في { الخناس } على وزان تعريف موصوفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Evil thoughts make a person hesitate and be checked by conscience, religion, shame, or fear, then recur until he accepts and becomes habituated to them; the whisperer alternately appears and withdraws until deception secures the act.
rows.anchor: ولأن خواطر الشر يهم بها صاحبها فيطرق ويتردد ويخاف تبعاتها وتزجره النفس اللوامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Who whispers in people’s breasts” makes the hidden process easier to recognize and guard against; breasts signify inner feeling, as in the cited Qurʾānic passages.
rows.anchor: ووصف { الوسواس الخناس } ب { الذي يوسوس في صدور الناس } لتقريب تصوير الوسوسة كي يتقيها المرء

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet defines sin as what troubles the breast and unsettles the heart; Ibn ʿĀshūr gives no grading for this report.
rows.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( الإثم ما حاك في الصدر وتردد في القلب )

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Among the Prophet’s analogies for satanic whispering is a kind of proboscis reaching into a person’s heart.
rows.anchor: أنها كالخراطيم يمدها الشيطان إلى قلب الإنسان

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Other Prophetic approximations compare whispering to nafth and to ibsās; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: مرة بالنفث ، ومرة بالإبساس

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says Satan moves through a human like blood and says he feared the devil might cast something into both listeners’ hearts; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: إن الشيطان يجري من ابن آدم مجرى الدم وإني خشيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Applying “whispers” to Satan is metaphorical because Satan does not literally speak inside a person, while a human persuading another toward evil is literal; the effect in breasts is literal for satanic whispering and causally attributed for human whispering.
rows.anchor: وإطلاق فعل { يوسوس } على هذا العمل الشيطاني مجاز إذ ليس للشيطان كلام في باطن الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition min is explanatory: the whisperer in people’s breasts divides into jinn, the original source, and humans, who follow and ally with them; the two are joined in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: من الجنة والناس } بيانية بينت { الذي يوسوس في صدور الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clarification matters because people readily guard against satanic whispers but may overlook human whisperers, whose danger is greater through their closeness, risk, and capacity to harm.
rows.anchor: أن من الوسواس ما هو شر من وسواس الشياطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min cannot explain al-nās as a word that includes jinn, since al-nās does not refer to jinn; that interpretation is far-fetched.
rows.anchor: ولا يستقيم أن يكون { من } بيانا للناس إذ لا يطلق اسم { الناس } على ما يشمل الجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jinn precede humans here because they are the original whisperers; al-Anʿām reverses the order because human enemies mixed more closely with prophets than satans did.
rows.anchor: وقدم { الجنة } على { الناس } هنا لأنهم أصل الوسواس كما علمت بخلاف تقديم الإنس على الجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God protects His prophets from satanic control so that revelation can be conveyed, citing the promise that Satan has no authority over God’s servants except followers among the straying.
rows.anchor: الله عصم أنبياءه من تسلط الشياطين على نفوسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets can still suffer human plots, as the conspiracy against the Prophet shows; God nevertheless guarantees messengers’ safety from anything that would prevent conveying the message until His purpose is fulfilled.
rows.anchor: ولم يعصمهم من لحاق ضر الناس بهم والكيد لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-jinnah is a collective noun formed from a singular jinnī by the adjectival nisba suffix, as insī is formed for an individual human.
rows.anchor: اسم جمع جني بياء النسب إلى نوع الجن ، فالجني الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first two repetitions of al-nās refer to the same humans; explicit naming instead of a pronoun stresses that God is Lord, King, and God of all people, as another Qurʾānic repetition illustrates.
rows.anchor: وتكرير كلمة { الناس } في هذه الآيات المرتين الأوليين باعتبار معنى واحد إظهار في مقام الإضمار لقصد تأكيد ربوبية الله تعالى وملكه وإلاهيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third occurrence of al-nās in “people’s breasts” is repeated explicitly because its referent is distant.
rows.anchor: فهو إظهار لأجل بعد المعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fourth al-nās, in “from jinn and people,” names the human class among the two kinds of whisperers, a different referent from the earlier occurrences.
rows.anchor: فلأنه بيان لأحد صنفي الذي يوسوس في صدور الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr closes by praying that God shield people from both groups’ evil and benefit them through the good of both weighty communities.
rows.anchor: والله يكفينا شر الفريقين ، وينفعنا
